title: The night director
story:
Final project 2. Every night shift is run by an unseen director that decides when the waving figures appear, announces midnight, and ends the night at dawn. To keep it testable, it doesn't use real time or real randomness: the game feeds it time with update, and gives it the random function to use.

This combines classes, state machines, loops, careful ordering and dependency injection.
create: A ModuleScript named `Director` inside it: a class created with `Director.new(settings, random)`.

requirements.text: `Director.new(settings, random)` takes `{ shiftLength, figureMin, figureMax }` and a function `random(low, high)` that returns a number of seconds. It starts at time 0 in state `"Evening"`, and immediately calls `random(figureMin, figureMax)` once to schedule the first figure. `getTime()` and `getState()` report time and state.

`update(seconds)` moves time forward and returns an array of the events that happened during that time, in time order. When the time reaches a scheduled figure, it adds `"figure"` and schedules the next one after another call to `random(figureMin, figureMax)`.
When time reaches half of `shiftLength`, it adds `"midnight"` once and the state becomes `"Midnight"`. A single update can contain several events, which must come out in the order they happened.
When time reaches `shiftLength`, it adds `"dawn"`, the state becomes `"Dawn"`, time stops at `shiftLength`, and later updates return no events.
A figure due at exactly the same moment as dawn doesn't happen: dawn wins. A figure due at the same moment as midnight comes first.

hints: Store the time of the next figure, rather than a countdown. Each update has a target time to reach.

Inside update, loop: work out which comes first, the next figure, midnight (if it hasn't happened) or dawn, and whether it's before the target time. Handle that one event, then repeat until nothing more happens before the target.
When dawn happens, record it and stop the loop, so nothing at or after dawn can fire.

static.fail: Create a ModuleScript named `Director` in the `Final2` folder.
Director should only use the random function it's given and the time passed to update, never real randomness or real time.

check:
local Director, info = Course.load("ServerScriptService.Course.Final2.Director")
if type(Director) ~= "table" or type(Director.new) ~= "function" then
	Course.fail("r2", "Director should return a class with a new function, but returned " .. Course.show(Director) .. (if info.error then " (" .. info.error .. ")" else ""))
	for _, id in { "r3", "r4", "r5", "r6" } do Course.fail(id, "Not checked: Director didn't load.") end
	return
end
local function sequence(values)
	local index = 0
	local asked = {}
	return function(low, high)
		index += 1
		table.insert(asked, { low, high })
		return values[(index - 1) % #values + 1]
	end, asked
end
local settings = { shiftLength = 100, figureMin = 10, figureMax = 20 }
local function make(values)
	local rng, asked = sequence(values)
	local good, director = Course.call(Director.new, table.clone(settings), rng)
	return director, asked
end
Course.try("r2", function()
	local director, asked = make({ 15 })
	Course.check("r2", type(director) == "table" and director:getState() == "Evening" and director:getTime() == 0, "A new director should start at time 0 in the \"Evening\" state.")
	Course.check("r2", #asked == 1 and asked[1][1] == 10 and asked[1][2] == 20, "When created, the director should ask its random function once for the first figure's wait, with the settings' figureMin and figureMax (10 and 20).")
end)
Course.try("r3", function()
	local director = make({ 15, 12, 18 })
	local events = {}
	for _ = 1, 8 do
		for _, e in director:update(5) do table.insert(events, e) end
	end
	Course.check("r3", Course.equal(events, { "figure", "figure" }), "With waits of 15 then 12, updating 5 seconds at a time for 40 seconds should fire a figure at 15 and 27 (and the next would be at 45). Got " .. Course.show(events))
	Course.check("r3", director:getTime() == 40, "getTime should be 40 after updates totalling 40 seconds.")
end)
Course.try("r4", function()
	local director = make({ 30 })
	local first = director:update(55)
	Course.check("r4", Course.equal(first, { "figure", "midnight" }), "Jumping 55 seconds at once with a wait of 30 should return the figure at 30 and midnight at 50, in time order: {\"figure\", \"midnight\"}. Got " .. Course.show(first))
	Course.check("r4", director:getState() == "Midnight", "After midnight the state should be \"Midnight\", but it's " .. Course.show(director:getState()))
	local second = director:update(10)
	Course.check("r4", Course.equal(second, { "figure" }), "The next figure is due at 60. Updating to 65 should return {\"figure\"} and not midnight again. Got " .. Course.show(second))
end)
Course.try("r5", function()
	local director = make({ 40 })
	local all = {}
	for _ = 1, 9 do
		for _, e in director:update(15) do table.insert(all, e) end
	end
	Course.check("r5", Course.equal(all, { "figure", "midnight", "figure", "dawn" }), "Updating 15 seconds at a time with waits of 40, events should be a figure at 40, midnight at 50, a figure at 80, then dawn at 100, and nothing after dawn. Got " .. Course.show(all))
	Course.check("r5", director:getState() == "Dawn" and director:getTime() == 100, "After dawn the state should be \"Dawn\" and time should stop at 100, but state is " .. Course.show(director:getState()) .. " and time is " .. Course.show(director:getTime()))
end)
Course.try("r6", function()
	local director = make({ 5 })
	local events = director:update(100)
	local figures = 0
	for _, e in events do
		if e == "figure" then figures += 1 end
	end
	Course.check("r6", figures == 19 and events[11] == "midnight" and events[#events] == "dawn" and #events == 21, "With a wait of 5 and one big 100-second update, figures fire at 5, 10 and so on up to 50, then midnight, then more figures, and dawn ends the night. A figure due at the same moment as dawn doesn't fire. Expected 19 figures in total, got " .. Course.show(events))
end)
steps: In the `Director` tab, make a class. `Director.new(settings, random)` gets `settings` like `{ shiftLength = 100, figureMin = 10, figureMax = 20 }`, and a function `random(low, high)` that returns a number of seconds. Never use `math.random`, `task.wait` or the clock.
When it's created: time is 0, the state is `"Evening"`, and it calls `random(figureMin, figureMax)` once to decide when the first figure appears.

`update(seconds)` moves time forward by that much, and returns a list of what happened, in time order. Add `"figure"` when a figure is due, then call random again to schedule the next one. Add `"midnight"` once, at half the shift length, and change the state to `"Midnight"`. Add `"dawn"` at the shift length, change the state to `"Dawn"`, and stop time there: later updates return `{}`.
Ties: a figure at the same moment as midnight comes first. A figure at the same moment as dawn never happens.
`getTime()` and `getState()` report where the night is.
example:
Shift length 100, every random wait 30:
update(55) gives { "figure", "midnight" }   (figure at 30, midnight at 50)
update(10) gives { "figure" }               (figure at 60)
